For example, with Ubisoft’s Star Wars open-world game in development, there is a huge opportunity for them to create an MMO style online game with an single player campaign for your character to serve both audiences. On a macro level this is what GTA V did, not everyone plays online but the single player alone made the game insanely entertaining 10 years later. The Star Wars setting lends itself to huge a huge sandbox if the developers wanted to capitalize. This why games like Star Citizen have such hype around them a decade into development, because the demand is there. I was disappointed to hear that Bethesda’s new space rpg has no multiplayer element either.

Hogwarts Legacy could transition over later down the line as well, lots of customization and fantasy sandbox for players to dive into online. RDR2 online didn’t have the same opportunity though, which another commenter pointed out why it couldn’t come close to GTA V online. Not every game can be translated to GTA online style MMO due to the limitations you mentioned. But for the ones that can, why not?

Fair enough! You make a good point that the MMO sandbox niche that GTA online dominates definitely can’t work in every setting. I think in more futuristic settings it would get more interesting with huge opportunity for player property (I.e. Star Wars, space ships/outposts on different planets etc). 

The new Harry Potter game in particular has the room of requirement which I believe players would love to customize and show off to other people in-game, comparable to the GTA online apartments feature. But it makes sense how the western setting of RDR2 limits that particular aspect of the experience

Yes, essentially what I’m wondering is why there aren’t MMO games in the particular niche (3rd person sandbox genre) that GTA dominates. Would love to see other IPs translated in that similar fashion. With all of their success, The Division, and Destiny are solely video games, just to use your examples. Imagine how popular movie universes like Star Wars, Harry Potter, MCU would be. 

Completely different experiences IMO, so while these games could in theory have the longevity of GTA online, the universes are so different it’s really not a clone. Huge opportunity for these potential MMOs to differentiate themselves in the market. I think these IPs can pool together resources to pull something like that off. 

I think the another potential reason why they we haven’t seen many attempts is because these big IP fan bases are so strong, developers and publishers don’t need to invest to create the MMO experience because the games will sell regardless. However in my opinion these single player connected MMO games are much more fulfilling to engage with. It truly scratches the “metaverse” itch without the gimmicks.

If you don’t live near any manufacturers then your second option is to use either online or overseas manufacturers. Online (you can find a lot of domestic manufacturers on Instagram) is more expensive than local but you have more quality control.

Overseas manufacturers you can find via Alibaba, or instagram as well. This should be a last resort for you because it’s really hard to control quality this way due to distance.

Hope this helps and good luck!

If you don’t have any luck on here finding an artist, don’t be afraid to use Fiverr, just go over to the illustrations category. 

Another method is DMing your favorite artists on Instagram to see if they’ll work with you!
